transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

I came in because… well, people kept telling me I should talk to someone, but the main thing is I keep hearing them. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off. It’s usually board members, staff, people saying I’m ruining the company.

And it’s not like a vague noise. It’s clear. Clear enough that I’ll answer back before I realize nobody else in the room heard anything. Then everyone looks at me like I’ve done something strange, but I swear it sounded right there.
How long have you been hearing these voices and having these experiences—did this start recently, like in the past few weeks, or has it been going on for months or longer?

It’s not just the last couple weeks. I mean, time gets strange when every day feels like a meeting that never actually ends, you know? But the voices—the ones from the walls, or my phone when it shouldn’t even be making noise—that’s been going on about three months now.

At first I thought it was just stress, or bad acoustics in the office, because conference rooms do that thing where sound carries funny. We had a room like that years ago too, with glass panels—terrible design choice. But no, this has been… about three months.

Over these past three months, have you noticed any big changes in your mood—like feeling unusually high-energy, irritable, or on top of the world, or on the other end, feeling deeply down, hopeless, or losing interest in things?

Not high-energy, no. I mean, I used to be high-energy in the normal way—running the room, pushing ideas, calling people after openings or meetings because I’d get excited about where things could go. I was always the one moving things forward.

Lately it’s more like… I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at the agenda and not really start anything. Which is ridiculous, because agendas used to be my favorite thing, color-coded sometimes—not that anyone appreciated that, but it kept everyone honest.

And I barely talk. To my staff, to my husband. It’s like the words are there but not worth the effort. Work used to feel like mine, like it mattered, and now I can look at it and feel almost nothing. Not exactly crying hopeless, just… blank.
You mentioned the voices started about three months ago—did this low energy and withdrawal from work and your husband start around that same time, or did it begin before or after the voices started?

It started before the voices, I think. Not all at once, not like a switch. It’s been building for… about two years and four months, if I’m being precise, since the expansion.

That was when they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division, which sounded glamorous, but it was really just three departments stapled together and everyone pretending the budget made sense. I remember because we had those awful launch folders with the silver lettering—completely unreadable under the lobby lights.

But yes, the pulling back, the energy going out of things… that started around then. The voices came much later.
During this past couple of years, have you also noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness, along with that 'blank' feeling?

I don’t know. I mean, sleep is such a slippery thing to measure, isn’t it? People ask that like there’s a simple number, but if you’re lying there thinking about tomorrow’s board packet, does that count as sleeping badly or just being responsible?

Appetite… I haven’t really kept track. We used to order lunch for the office from that Mediterranean place on Sixth—terrible hummus, honestly, but everyone acted like it was special because it came in those little compostable bowls. I remember eating it, or moving it around, I guess.

Guilt or worthlessness… I don’t know. I wouldn’t call it that exactly. Blank is still the better word. Like the volume got turned down on everything, but I can’t tell you if that’s guilt or just… nothing.
Have there been any times in the past three months when you heard the voices or felt people were against you, but your mood and energy actually felt normal—not blank or low?

I mean… normal is hard to say. There are moments where I’m just doing the usual things—checking emails, sitting in the conference room, looking at the quarterly packet—and then I hear them. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off.

It’s usually board members, or staff, saying I’m ruining the company. Very clear. Not like a thought. Clear enough that I’ll answer them, and then realize no one else reacted.

So I don’t know if my mood felt “normal,” exactly, but it wasn’t always that blank feeling first. Sometimes the voices just… happened. Like they came into the room before I did, if that makes sense.

In the past three months, was there ever a stretch of at least two full weeks where you were hearing the voices but did NOT have that blank, low, withdrawn feeling—where your mood and energy felt essentially back to your normal self while the voices were still happening?

I don’t know about a clean two-week stretch. It’s hard to sort it like that because the voices don’t seem to care what mood I’m in.

That’s really why I came in—because I keep hearing people talking about me, through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off. Usually board members or staff, saying I’m ruining the company. And it sounds so clear that I’ll answer them before I realize no one else heard anything.

The “blank” feeling is there a lot, but I can’t honestly map it neatly against the voices. The voices just happen.
Since the voices started three months ago, would you say that blank, withdrawn feeling has been present most of the time, or has it only been there some of the days since then?

Most of the time, I think. Not every single minute, because that sounds too neat, but… it’s been there more often than not.

I used to be the one pushing everything forward—new ideas, calling people after openings, keeping everyone moving. Now I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at the agenda like it’s written in another language. And then someone knocks and I realize I haven’t said anything all morning.

Even at home, I barely talk to my husband. At work I barely talk to staff unless I have to. It’s strange because I used to love all of it, or I thought I did, and now I just feel… almost nothing.

Yeah… most of the time, it’s that blank thing. I used to be the one driving every idea, you know? Calling people after openings, pushing projects, making sure everyone was moving. I had this whole notebook system—well, three notebooks, actually, because one was for the restaurant side and one was for staffing and then one I kept losing in my car—

But now I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at the agenda. Like I know the words are there, but I don’t… connect to them. And I barely speak unless someone makes me. At home, too, with my husband, I just don’t have anything to say.

It’s not even sadness exactly. It’s more like I feel almost nothing about work I used to love.
Compared to before this began, have you noticed you're sleeping noticeably more, or noticeably less, than you used to?

I don’t know if I could say more or less in a clear way. I haven’t really been tracking it.

Some nights I’m in bed and it feels like I’ve been there forever, but then I don’t know if I actually slept or just lay there thinking about stupid things, like whether I sent an email to the caterer from two years ago—well, not two years, maybe last spring. And then other times I’m up and it’s morning and I can’t remember when I fell asleep.

So… noticeably? I’m not sure. It’s not something I can measure cleanly.

I’m not really sure. I mean, I get into bed, but I don’t know if that counts as sleeping, you know? My husband has one of those little sleep apps on his phone, but I don’t use things like that because then I start looking at all the numbers and it becomes this whole other project.

So… compared to before, I can’t honestly say it’s clearly more or clearly less. It just feels kind of hard to tell.

Going back further in your life, before these past two years, was there ever a stretch of several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if nothing like that is happening now?

I’m not sure I’d know how to separate that from just… being busy. I mean, when we were opening locations, everybody was running around on coffee and bad sandwiches, and I’d stay late because someone had to sign off on invoices or the flower delivery got sent to the wrong entrance—things like that.

But unusually elated or like I didn’t need sleep? I don’t know. I can’t think of a clear stretch like that off the top of my head. It’s hard to say what was “unusual” versus just the job being what it was.

Before the voices started three months ago, during that two-year period of feeling withdrawn and 'blank,' did you ever find yourself suspicious of coworkers or believe people were plotting against you or the company, even without actually hearing anything?

I don’t know. “Plotting” sounds so… dramatic, like a movie boardroom with people whispering behind glass walls. Work always had people talking, and sometimes I’d walk into a room and the conversation would stop, but that happens when you’re the boss too. It doesn’t always mean anything.

I mean, I probably wondered what people were saying about me, or about decisions, because people always have opinions. There was this one operations meeting where the seating chart got changed—sorry, that’s not really related. It’s just, little things at work could feel loaded sometimes.

But before the voices, I can’t say I had a clear belief that coworkers were plotting against me or the company. Not in a way I could point to and say, yes, that was definitely happening.

Before this current stretch of feeling blank and withdrawn started about two years ago, had you ever gone through a separate period earlier in your life—weeks or months long—where you felt similarly down, low-energy, or withdrawn, and then fully returned to your normal self afterward?

I don’t know… earlier than two years ago, it all feels sort of mixed together. I had stressful stretches, sure—work could swallow whole seasons if you let it. There was one winter where we were dealing with vendor contracts and I remember barely seeing daylight, but that might’ve just been because my office didn’t have good windows.

But weeks or months where I was clearly down and then bounced back to normal? I’m not sure I can point to something like that. I mean, people change over time, right? Normal is kind of a moving target.

doctor.question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I am returning the chief complaint symptom code S020.

patient.answer:
I came in because… well, people kept telling me I should talk to someone, but the main thing is I keep hearing them. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off. It’s usually board members, staff, people saying I’m ruining the company.

And it’s not like a vague noise. It’s clear. Clear enough that I’ll answer back before I realize nobody else in the room heard anything. Then everyone looks at me like I’ve done something strange, but I swear it sounded right there.

doctor.question: How long have you been hearing these voices and having these experiences—did this start recently, like in the past few weeks, or has it been going on for months or longer?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices from the walls or my phone have been happening for about the past 3 months.

It’s not just the last couple weeks. I mean, time gets strange when every day feels like a meeting that never actually ends, you know? But the voices—the ones from the walls, or my phone when it shouldn’t even be making noise—that’s been going on about three months now.
